steps.body: You already move waves UP (midline) and STRETCH them (amplitude, period). The last motion is SIDEWAYS: y = sin(x − C) slides the whole wave **C to the right** — the **phase shift**. Inside the parentheses, minus means right (the same inside-flip as every function shift).

predict.prompt: y = sin(x − 90°) is sin x with its start delayed. Where is its FIRST peak?

options.label: Still at 90° — shifting doesn't move the peak
At 180° — everything slides right by the shift
At 0° — the wave starts at its top now

predict.reveal: 180°. The circle's pointer starts 90° behind, so every feature of the wave — peak included — arrives 90° late. Drag θ and watch the trace: the peak lands where the pointer finally reaches the top.

widget.prompt: The circle starts 90° behind (phase −90°) and traces y = sin(x − 90°) as you drag. Land the trace on the wave's first peak.
widget.successFeedback: Peak at 180° — which is π in the prose above, the answer n = 1. The peak moved because the circle STARTED elsewhere: the wave slides exactly as far as the start was delayed.
widget.lowFeedback: Not there yet — 90° is where PLAIN sin x peaks, but this pointer started 90° behind and hasn't reached the top. Keep dragging and watch the point climb.
widget.highFeedback: Past the peak — the trace is already on its way down. Back up until the tip sits on the crest, where the pointer is at the very top of the circle.

explanationVariants: y = sin(x + π/3) has C = −π/3: the wave slides LEFT by π/3 — plus inside means left.
The wave hits sin's zero start where x + π/3 = 0, i.e. x = −π/3: shifted left.

widget.prompt: The graph of y = sin(x + π/3) is the sine wave shifted:

options.label: left by π/3
options.feedback: Right — inside PLUS is a LEFT slide, the mirror of every inside shift you've seen.

options.label: right by π/3
options.feedback: Right needs a MINUS inside: sin(x − π/3). Plus inside pre-loads the input, pulling the wave left.

options.label: up by π/3
options.feedback: Vertical moves live OUTSIDE the function (… + π/3 at the end). Inside changes are horizontal.

steps.body: With a period change, read the shift ONLY after factoring: y = sin(2x − π/3) = sin(2(x − **π/6**)) — the shift is π/6, not π/3. The B multiplies the whole inside, so the raw constant overstates the slide by a factor of B.

explanationVariants: 4x − π = 4(x − π/4): the phase shift is π/4 right.
Divide the constant by B: π ÷ 4 = π/4.

widget.prompt: What is the phase shift of y = sin(4x − π)?

options.label: π/4 right
options.feedback: Right — factoring gives sin(4(x − π/4)): the slide is the constant DIVIDED by B.

options.label: π right
options.feedback: π is the unfactored constant. B = 4 compresses it: the true shift is π/4.

options.label: π/4 left
options.feedback: The factored form has a MINUS: 4(x − π/4) — minus inside slides right.

explanationVariants: At x = 5π/12: 2x − π/3 = 5π/6 − 2π/6 = π/2, and sin(π/2) = 1 — a peak, confirming the shifted wave crests π/6 late (at π/4 + π/6 = 5π/12).
The peak solves 2x − π/3 = π/2: x = (π/2 + π/3)/2 = 5π/12.

widget.prompt: y = 2 sin(2x − π/3). What is y at x = 5π/12?

commonErrors.feedback: The AMPLITUDE is 2: at a peak the value is the full 2, since sin hits exactly 1.
x = 5π/12 makes the inside π/2 — a PEAK, not a zero: y = 2·1 = 2.

steps.body: All the pieces of the inside.
explanationVariants: Factor: 3x + π/2 = 3(x + π/6): shift π/6 LEFT. n = 6.
Constant over B: (π/2)/3 = π/6, and the + sign means left.
hints: Factor B = 3 out of the inside.
Plus inside means left; the size is π/6.

widget.prompt: y = sin(3x + π/2) is shifted LEFT by π/n. What is n?

commonErrors.feedback: π/2 is the raw constant. Factor out B = 3: the true shift is (π/2)/3 = π/6, so n = 6.
3 is B, the period-changer. The shift divides the constant by it: π/6 → n = 6.

takeaways: sin(x − C): slide right C; plus inside slides left.
With a B, factor first — shift = constant ÷ B.
Verify any shift by tracking one landmark point.
steps.teaser: Next: stacking all four motions into one wave.

concept.body: Phase shift = the C in sin(B(x − C)). Get there by factoring B out of the inside; minus → right, plus → left.

explanationVariants: Constant π over B = 2: π/2, minus sign → right.

widget.prompt: The phase shift of y = sin(2x − π) is:

options.label: π right
options.feedback: Factor the 2 first: the shift is π/2, half the raw constant.

options.label: π/2 left
options.feedback: The factored inside is (x − π/2): minus slides right.
